name: Shareholder Entry Permits (Trade, Professional Services, Agriculture/Mining/Manufacturing)

requirements.blocker_text: Shareholder in a company engaged in general trade, holding a valid trading license.

Shareholder in a company engaged in a specific licensed profession (medicine, dentistry, law, pharmacy, engineering, accountancy, architecture, surveying, veterinary science, estate agency, valuation, nursing/midwifery), holding registration with the relevant Ugandan professional body.

requirement_groups.name: Agriculture, Mining, or Manufacturing (Classes B1/B2, C1/C2, E)

requirements.blocker_text: Shareholder in a company engaged in agriculture, agro-processing, mining, or manufacturing, holding a Uganda Investment Authority (UIA) investment license.
Minimum US$250,000 capital investment (foreign-investor threshold; US$50,000 for domestic investors).
requirements.fix_path: Invest at least US$250,000 in the qualifying enterprise.

evidence_required.document: Ministry of Agriculture approval (agriculture sector only)

outcome.duration_length: 6 months (USD 1,250-1,500), 12 months (USD 2,500-3,000), 24 months (USD 5,000-6,000), or 36 months (USD 7,500-9,000) depending on class, all beyond 6 months including a USD 1,500 non-refundable component

sources.title: Directorate of Citizenship and Immigration Control, Uganda -- Class D Entry Permit (General Trade shareholders): USD 1,250 (6mo) to 7,500 (36mo), requires trading license, agency letter, tax clearance, 3 months' bank statements

Directorate of Citizenship and Immigration Control, Uganda -- Class F Entry Permit (Professional Services shareholders): USD 1,500 (6mo) to 9,000 (36mo), requires proof of registration with the relevant Ugandan professional body

Uganda Investment Authority (UIA) -- Getting Started: investment license issued within 48 hours via the eBiz portal if criteria met, free of charge; minimum capital US$50,000 (domestic investors) / US$250,000 (foreign investors); UIA license is a prerequisite for Class B (agriculture), C (mining), and E (manufacturing) entry permits, though foreign nationals must still separately apply for the entry permit itself through DCIC

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Uganda). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- all three requirement groups tier-1 sourced (two directly fetched by me: Class D and the UIA getting-started page). This dataset consolidates Uganda's numerous sector-specific shareholder permit classes (B1/B2 agriculture/agro-processing, C1/C2 mining, D general trade, E manufacturing, F professional services) into one file with requirement_groups by sector, rather than 6 near-identical files differing mainly in sector documentation -- consistent with this dataset's approach elsewhere (e.g. Nigeria's investor tiers). Class F is a genuinely distinctive structural finding: it is nominally a 'professional' permit but is legally structured as a SHAREHOLDER class like the others, not an individual practicing-professional work permit -- a foreign doctor or lawyer must hold a stake in a Ugandan company in that field, not merely be employed by one (ordinary employed professionals would instead use ug_work_permit.json's Class G2). citizenship_after_months cross-referenced from ug_citizenship_by_residence.json, not independently sourced here.
